heroData.title: Hire in Korea (No Entity)
heroData.subtitle: 52-Hour Rule
heroData.description: Strict enforcement of 52-hour work week (40 standard + 12 overtime). EOR handles '4 Major Insurances' and local compliance.

steps.title: Contractual Definition
steps.description: Drafting the labor contract in Korean (bilingual recommended). Must explicitly define base salary, meal allowance (usually KRW 100,000-200,000 tax-free), and overtime components to comply with the 52-hour rule.

steps.title: 4 Major Insurances Acquisition
steps.description: Reporting the 'Acquisition of Eligibility' for National Pension, Health, Employment, and Workers' Compensation insurance within 14 days of the start date.

steps.title: Rules of Employment (ROE)
steps.description: If the EOR unit or client site has 10+ employees, the ROE must be filed with the Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL). Employees must be notified of these rules.

steps.title: Anti-Harassment Training
steps.description: Setting up mandatory annual training sessions for workplace sexual harassment prevention and disability awareness, as required by law.

steps.title: Time Tracking Integration
steps.description: Implementing a digital attendance system to monitor the 40+12 hour limit. Any hours beyond 52/week are strictly prohibited and carry criminal liability for the employer.

items.title: 52-Hour Work Week
items.text: Total working hours cannot exceed 52 per week (40 standard + 12 overtime). Violations can lead to imprisonment for the CEO/Representative.

items.title: Severance Pay (Toijikgeum)
items.text: Employees who work >1 year are entitled to 30 days of average salary for every year worked. EORs typically accrue this monthly to avoid large liabilities.

items.title: Paid Holidays
items.text: Public holidays are now mandatory paid rest days for all companies with 5+ employees. If employees work on a holiday, they must receive 150% pay or compensatory leave.

items.title: Pregnancy Protection
items.text: Female employees are entitled to 90 days of maternity leave (120 for twins), with 60 days paid by the employer and 30 by employment insurance.

items.title: Childcare Leave
items.text: Employees with children under age 8 can request up to 1 year of unpaid or partially subsidized leave. Retaliation for taking leave is strictly forbidden.

faqs.question: Can I terminate an employee during probation?
faqs.answer: Yes, usually within the first 3 months with a 30-day notice or payment in lieu. However, 'just cause' is still highly scrutinized by Labor Commissions.

faqs.question: Are 13th-month bonuses mandatory?
faqs.answer: No, they are not statutory. However, many Korean companies provide performance-based incentives or 'Chuseok/Lunar New Year' bonuses.

faqs.question: Does the EOR handle the '4 insurances'?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is the primary benefit of using an EOR. They manage the monthly reporting and payments to the National Pension, Health, Employment, and Workers' Compensation services.

items.title: LSA (Labor Standards Act)
items.text: The primary law governing employment conditions, wages, and working hours in South Korea.

items.title: Toijikgeum
items.text: Statutory severance pay. Usually accrued in a retirement pension fund (DB or DC type).

items.title: Gwageup
items.text: Excess work or overtime. Must be precisely tracked and compensated at 150% rate.

items.title: Wages of Employment
items.text: Includes base salary + fixed allowances (meal, vehicle). Used for social insurance calculations.

items.title: MOEL
items.text: Ministry of Employment and Labor, the regulatory body enforcing labor laws and conducting inspections.

steps.title: Data Collection
steps.description: Finalize overtime hours, meal allowances, and any variable bonuses. Deadline usually by the 20th.

steps.title: Calculation & Withholding
steps.description: Calculate progressive income tax (withholding) and the 4 Major Insurance premiums based on the 2025 rates.

steps.title: Payment & Payslips
steps.description: Distribute net pay and provide detailed payslips (Myeongseoseo) indicating all deduction items clearly.

steps.title: Tax Filing (10th)
steps.description: Report and pay the withheld income tax and local income tax to the NTS by the 10th of the following month.

items.title: Year-End Tax Adjustment (YETA)
items.text: Conducted in February. Employees submit medical/educational receipts to NTS to recalculate actual tax liability vs. withheld amounts.

items.title: Tax-Free Allowances
items.text: Meal allowances up to KRW 200,000/month and child care allowances up to KRW 200,000 are exempt from income tax and social insurance.

items.title: CEO Liability
items.text: Under the Serious Accidents Punishment Act (SAPA), payroll and safety budgets must be properly allocated to avoid personal liability for executives.

items.title: Insurance Caps
items.text: National Pension and Health Insurance have maximum monthly wage caps. For 2024/2025, the Pension cap is KRW 6.17M and Health is KRW 110.3M.

items.title: Bonus Withholding
items.text: Bonuses are taxed at the same progressive rates as monthly salary but may lead to higher withholding in the month of payment.

faqs.question: What is the '10th of the month' deadline?
faqs.answer: It is the strict deadline for paying withheld income tax and social insurance premiums for the previous month's payroll.

faqs.question: How is overtime calculated?
faqs.answer: Overtime, night shifts (22:00-06:00), and holiday work must be paid at 150% of the normal hourly base.

items.title: 6% Rate
items.text: Taxable income up to KRW 14M per year.

items.title: 15% Rate
items.text: Taxable income between KRW 14M and KRW 50M.

items.title: 24% Rate
items.text: Taxable income between KRW 50M and KRW 88M.

items.title: Max 45% Rate
items.text: For income exceeding KRW 1B per year.

steps.title: Monthly Base Salary
steps.description: Enter the gross monthly amount including fixed monthly allowances.

steps.title: Dependents Count
steps.description: Used to determine the progressive income tax withholding bracket (Simplification Table).

steps.title: Tax-Free Items
steps.description: Deducting KRW 200,000 for meal allowance to lower the taxable base.

items.title: Rounding Rules
items.text: Deductions in Korea are typically rounded to the nearest 10 KRW to avoid unit issues.

items.title: Variable Overtime
items.text: The calculator assumes a standard 40-hour week. Actual net pay will vary significantly with tracked overtime at 1.5x.

items.title: Local Income Tax
items.text: Calculated as 10% of the National Income Tax. It is filed separately but usually together with the main withholding report.

items.title: D-8 Visa Tax Rates
items.text: Foreign engineers/executives may qualify for a 19% flat tax rate on their gross income, bypassing the progressive brackets.

faqs.question: How accurate is this estimate?
faqs.answer: The estimate is based on standard 2025 social insurance rates. Factors like industry-specific workers' comp rates can cause small variations (0.1-0.2%).

faqs.question: Does this include the local income tax?
faqs.answer: Yes, it calculates the base income tax and adds the 10% local income tax surcharge automatically.

faqs.question: Are year-end adjustments included?
faqs.answer: The calculator provides a monthly snapshot. Year-end tax adjustments (YETA) are typically handled in February and may result in a refund or additional tax based on 12-month spending/savings.

items.title: Meal Allowance
items.text: KRW 200,000 threshold. Any amount above this is treated as taxable salary.

items.title: Vehicle Allowance
items.text: Up to KRW 200,000 is tax-free if the employee uses their private vehicle for company business.

items.title: Severance Accumulation
items.text: Accrual of 1/12th of annual salary per work year. Must be paid within 14 days of termination.

items.title: Night Shift Premium
items.text: Work between 10 PM and 6 AM requires an additional 50% of base hourly wage.

items.title: Holiday Work Pay
items.text: Working on a statutory holiday or Sunday requires 150% pay (200% if >8 hours).

items.title: Childcare Allowance
items.text: Up to KRW 200,000 per month is tax-free for employees with children under 6.

items.title: Overseas Allowance
items.text: Special tax-free thresholds exist for employees working abroad or on deep-sea vessels.

items.title: Invention Compensation
items.text: Tax-free limits apply to rewards paid for employee-designed patents or improvements.

items.title: Small Business Tax Break
items.text: Youth employees (aged 15-34) at SMEs may qualify for up to 90% income tax reduction.

items.title: Commuter Housing Fund
items.text: Employer-provided housing support may be non-taxable under specific relocation conditions.

heroData.title: Chusik Hoesa (JSC)
heroData.subtitle: Standard Corp
heroData.description: Most common structure (Joint Stock Company). Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) also exists but less common for FDI.

steps.title: FDI Notification
steps.description: Report the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) to a designated foreign exchange bank in Korea before remitting capital.

steps.title: Capital Remittance
steps.description: Remit at least KRW 100M (typical for D-8 visa) to a temporary 'escrow' account at the bank. Obtain a certificate of deposit.

steps.title: Court Registration
steps.description: Register the 'Chusik Hoesa' (JSC) with the local court registry. Requires physical corporate seal (Ingam) and notarized docs.

steps.title: Tax Registration
steps.description: Apply for a Business Registration Certificate at the local Tax Office. A physical lease agreement is usually required.

steps.title: FDI Company Reg
steps.description: Register the company as a foreign-invested enterprise at the bank to facilitate future dividend repatriation.

items.title: Seoul Metro Surcharge
items.text: Incorporating in the Seoul Metropolitan Area (including Gwangju, Incheon) triggers a 3x surcharge on the education/registration tax.

items.title: Chusik vs Yuhan
items.text: Chusik Hoesa (JSC) is the most prestigious for local hires and banks. Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) is simpler for US-based parents but can be seen as less stable.

items.title: Virtual Offices
items.text: Acceptable for the Registry in some cases, but the Tax Office may reject Business Registration without a specific physical footprint or sub-lease.

items.title: Branch vs Subsidiary
items.text: A branch is not a separate legal entity and may be easier to set up but harder to participate in local government tenders.

items.title: Capital Requirements
items.text: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) status requires minimum KRW 100M per investor to qualify for D-8 visa benefits.

faqs.question: What is the 'Ingam'?
faqs.answer: The official corporate seal. It is used to sign all major contracts and tax documents. Losing it is a major security and operations risk.

faqs.question: Can I set up a branch instead?
faqs.answer: Yes, but a Branch Office cannot engage in 'Foreign Direct Investment' incentives and has limited scope for hiring international staff (D-8 vs D-7).

faqs.question: What is the minimum capital?
faqs.answer: Technically KRW 1. However, to qualify for a foreign investor visa (D-8), a minimum of KRW 100M is required.

items.title: Notarized POA
items.text: Required for foreign shareholders who cannot be physically present for registry.

items.title: Bank Passbook
items.text: Essential for all local transactions; obtained after Business Registration.

items.title: Articles of Incorporation
items.text: Must be tailored to include specific business purposes (Upjong) to avoid tax issues.

items.title: Seal Certificate Renewal
items.text: Periodic renewal of corporate seal certificates is required for various government and banking filings.

items.title: Director Appointments
items.text: Standard terms are 3 years. Re-election or replacement must be registered within 2 weeks of the term end.

items.title: Annual Shareholder Meeting
items.text: Must be held within 3 months of the fiscal year end to approve financial statements and dividends.

items.title: Business License Update
items.text: Any change in office address or business scope requires a license update at the local tax office within 15-30 days.

heroData.title: Recruitment
heroData.subtitle: Competition
heroData.description: Fierce war for talent in Pangyo (Technovalley). Global brands preferred by candidates.

steps.title: Job Specification
steps.description: Defining the role. Note: Age/Gender discrimination in job ads is strictly prohibited and can lead to fines under the Equal Employment Opportunity Act.

steps.title: Sourcing Channels
steps.description: Posting on major portals: LinkedIn is preferred for tech/global roles, while Saramin and JobKorea are the dominant domestic players.

steps.title: Data Processing Consent
steps.description: Obtaining explicit consent under PIPA (Personal Information Protection Act) before collecting or storing candidate resumes.

steps.title: Technical Assessment
steps.description: Coding tests or technical interviews. Korean candidates increasingly value transparent feedback processes.

steps.title: Final Offer & Seal
steps.description: Extending the offer. Contracts are often signed using the company seal (Ingam) and employee's personal seal (Dojang) or signature.

items.title: Pangyo Techno Valley
items.text: The 'Silicon Valley' of Korea. High concentration of tech talent but extremely high turnover and salary inflation.

items.title: Background Checks
items.text: Criminal record checks are restricted to specific industries (e.g., security, education). General employers cannot request them without a clear legal basis.

items.title: Brand Recognition
items.text: Korean candidates often prioritize established global brands or high-growth 'Unicorns' over early-stage foreign startups.

items.title: The 'Hoe-sik' Culture
items.text: While declining, team dinners (Hoe-sik) are still part of the onboarding and bonding process. Modern companies lean towards lunches.

items.title: MBTI Phenomenon
items.text: MBTI is currently massive in Korea. Some job ads jokingly (or semi-seriously) mention preferred MBTI types, though not legally binding.

faqs.question: Are non-compete clauses valid in Korea?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they must be limited in scope, duration (usually 1 year), and geographical area. Courts often require the employer to provide compensation for the non-compete.

faqs.question: What is 'Rocket Punch'?
faqs.answer: Korea's leading startup-focused job platform, essential for hiring developers and early-stage employees.

items.title: Saramin
items.text: The most widely used general recruitment platform in South Korea.

items.title: JobKorea
items.text: Strong alternative to Saramin with a large database of experienced professionals.

items.title: Wanted
items.text: Referral-based platform highly popular among the tech and creative communities.

heroData.title: HR Software
heroData.subtitle: Attendance Tracking
heroData.description: Accurate time-tracking is mandatory for 52-hour week compliance.

steps.title: Compliance Mapping
steps.description: Configuring the system to handle the 52-hour work week, including automated alerts for overtime limits.

steps.title: PIPA Audit
steps.description: Ensuring the HRIS provider complies with the Personal Information Protection Act, particularly regarding data residency and encryption.

steps.title: Leave Policy Setup
steps.description: Automating the calculation of statutory annual leave (base 15 days + 1 day for every 2 years of service).

steps.title: Employee Self-Service
steps.description: Launching the mobile app/portal for attendance marking and payslip viewing, mandatory for transparency under the LSA.

items.title: Mobile Attendance
items.text: GPS and Wi-Fi based clocking is the norm in Korea to prevent 'buddy clocking' and ensure 52-hour compliance.

items.title: Data Shredding
items.text: HRIS systems must support permanent deletion of data once the statutory retention period (usually 3 years for payroll) expires.

items.title: Messenger Integration
items.text: Systems that integrate with KakaoTalk for notifications and approvals have much higher employee adoption rates in Korea.

faqs.question: Is digital attendance mandatory?
faqs.answer: While not strictly 'digital,' companies must provide accurate records of working hours. Digital systems are the only practical way to defend against 52-hour violations.

faqs.question: Can we use a global HRIS in Korea?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it must be localized for the '4 Major Insurances' and the complex statutory leave calculations unique to Korean LSA.

faqs.question: How does HRIS handle 'Toijikgeum'?
faqs.answer: Most local HRIS systems include a severance calculator that automatically tracks service days and average wages to estimate the liability.

items.title: 52-Hour Monitoring
items.text: The system must have a dashboard showing real-time 'Overtime Balance' for all 5+ employee units.

items.title: PIPA Certification
items.text: Verify if the provider has ISMS (Information Security Management System) certification in Korea.

items.title: Employee Consent
items.text: Digital logs for employee consent to collect biometric or GPS data for attendance.

heroData.title: Bookkeeping
heroData.subtitle: E-Tax Invoices
heroData.description: Mandatory Electronic Tax Invoices required for VAT. Strict NTS compliance.

steps.title: E-Tax Invoice Audit
steps.description: Reconciling all sales and purchases via the 'HomeTax' (NTS) portal. All business-to-business invoices MUST be electronic.

steps.title: Expense Voucher Mgt
steps.description: Collecting physical or digital receipts for corporate card transactions. Strict documentation is required for tax deductibility.

steps.title: VAT Preparation
steps.description: Consolidating input and output VAT for the quarterly filing (Jan, April, July, Oct).

steps.title: Monthly Close
steps.description: Generating the P&L and Balance Sheet for headquarters reporting. GAAP to IFRS conversions if necessary.

items.title: Electronic Tax Invoices
items.text: Mandatory for all corporations. Failure to issue an e-invoice carries a 1-2% penalty on the transaction value.

items.title: NTS Monitoring
items.text: The National Tax Service (NTS) has one of the most advanced digital monitoring systems in the world. Discrepancies often trigger automated inquiries.

items.title: Corporate Cards
items.text: Using corporate cards for all business expenses simplifies accounting as the data flows directly into the tax portal.

faqs.question: What is the accounting year in Korea?
faqs.answer: The standard fiscal year is Jan 1 to Dec 31. Companies can elect a different year in their Articles of Incorporation, but 95%+ follow the calendar year.

faqs.question: Is an external audit mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, for companies exceeding certain thresholds (e.g., assets > KRW 12B, liabilities > KRW 7B, or employees > 100).

items.title: HomeTax ID
items.text: The gateway to all tax and accounting reporting. Digital certificates are required for login.

items.title: Corporate Seal
items.text: Must match the registry to validate financial documents and bank transactions.

steps.title: Rules of Employment (ROE)
steps.description: Mandatory for companies with 10+ employees. Must be filed with the MOEL (Ministry of Employment and Labor).

steps.title: Occupational Safety
steps.description: Establishing a safety management system to comply with SAPA and the Industrial Safety and Health Act (ISHA).

steps.title: Sexual Harassment Prevention
steps.description: Conducting mandatory annual training for all employees. Records must be kept for 3 years.

steps.title: Data Protection Officer
steps.description: Appointing a CPO (Chief Privacy Officer) if the company processes personal data of Korean citizens under PIPA.

items.title: Serious Accidents Punishment Act
items.text: CEOs can face 1+ years in prison and the company up to KRW 5B in fines for fatal workplace accidents due to safety negligence.

items.title: Workplace Harassment
items.text: The LSA strictly prohibits 'gapjil' (abuse of power). Employers must investigate all claims immediately or face criminal penalties.

items.title: Disability Hiring
items.text: Companies with 50+ employees must meet disability hiring quotas or pay a monthly levy (solidarity contribution).

items.title: Sexual Harassment Training
items.text: Annual mandatory training for all employees. Documented proof must be kept for audits.

items.title: Privacy (PIPA)
items.text: Personal Information Protection Act requires explicit consent for cross-border data transfers of employee data.

faqs.question: What is the 52-hour work week rule?
faqs.answer: The maximum working hours are 40 standard hours plus 12 overtime hours. Violations carry up to 2 years in prison for the representative director.

faqs.question: How often are MOEL audits conducted?
faqs.answer: Routine audits are periodic, but 'Special Labor Inspections' occur if multiple complaints are filed or serious violations are suspected.

faqs.question: What is 'Gapjil'?
faqs.answer: A Korean term for workplace harassment or abuse of power. Anti-Gapjil laws are strictly enforced with mandatory investigation requirements.

items.title: Labor Inspectorate Kit
items.text: Maintaining a binder with Labor Contracts, ROE, Salary Register, and Training logs for MOEL visits.

items.title: SAPA Management Plan
items.text: Annual review of safety budgets and appointment of a safety officer (if 50+ staff).

items.title: PIPA Data Privacy
items.text: Ensuring PII is not sent overseas without explicit separate consent (Standard for global HQs).

steps.title: Self-Audit
steps.description: Reviewing all labor contracts and rules of employment for compliance with the latest LSA updates.

steps.title: Training Verification
steps.description: Ensuring all mandatory trainings (Sexual Harassment, Privacy, Disability) are completed and signed off.

steps.title: Document Filing
steps.description: Organizing payroll ledgers and attendance records for the mandatory 3-year retention period.

steps.title: VAT Filing
steps.description: Quarterly submission (April, July, Oct, Jan) for the respective previous quarter's activity.

steps.title: CIT Return
steps.description: Corporate Income Tax filing by March 31st for the previous calendar year.

steps.title: CIT Interim
steps.description: Payment of 50% of the previous year's tax or actual H1 results by August 31st.

steps.title: Global Reporting
steps.description: Filing the Master/Local file for Transfer Pricing if intercompany transactions exceed thresholds.

items.title: Expat Flat Tax
items.text: Foreign employees can elect a 19% flat income tax rate for their first 20 years of working in Korea, bypassing progressive brackets.

items.title: R&D Credits
items.text: Korea offers one of the world's most generous R&D tax credits, often reaching 25-50% for SMEs and 2-15% for large corps.

items.title: Transfer Pricing
items.text: Strict enforcement on management fees and royalty payments to parent companies. Must be at 'arm's length' terms.

faqs.question: What is the VAT rate in Korea?
faqs.answer: The standard VAT rate is 10%. Exported goods and certain international services have a 0% rate.

faqs.question: Are there tax holidays for foreign investors?
faqs.answer: Yes, localized incentives exist in Free Economic Zones (FEZs) for specific industries like high-tech and biotech.

faqs.question: What is the 'Local Income Tax'?
faqs.answer: An additional 10% surcharge on the Corporate Income Tax (CIT) amount, paid to the local municipal office.

items.title: Business Registration
items.text: Must be updated within 20 days if any business purpose or office location changes.

items.title: HomeTax Access
items.text: Ensure the 'Joint Certificate' (Gongdong Injeungseo) is renewed annually for NTS access.

items.title: Withholding Evidence
items.text: Maintaining records of all 3.3% freelancer tax and 10th-of-month salary tax payments.

heroData.title: Contracts
heroData.subtitle: Korean Law
heroData.description: Contracts should be bilingual. Korean version prevails in court.

steps.title: Bilingual Drafting
steps.description: Drafting contracts in both English and Korean. Ensure a 'governing language' clause specifies Korean for local courts.

steps.title: Jurisdiction Check
steps.description: Typically choosing the Seoul Central District Court or the Korean Commercial Arbitration Board (KCAB) for disputes.

steps.title: Seal Certificate
steps.description: Verifying the counterparty's corporate seal certificate (Ingam Jung-myeong-seo) to ensure the signer has authority.

faqs.question: Are electronic signatures legally binding in Korea?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the Digital Signature Act. However, major real estate or government-related filings often still require a physical seal (Ingam).

faqs.question: What is the KCAB?
faqs.answer: The Korean Commercial Arbitration Board. It is the only authorized institution in Korea for settling commercial disputes via arbitration.

faqs.question: Do contracts need to be notarized?
faqs.answer: Generally no for standard B2B services, but powers of attorney and certain corporate resolutions for the registry must be notarized and apostilled.

items.title: Termination Notice
items.text: Always specify a fixed notice period (e.g., 3 months) to align with statutory labor protections if the MSA involves dedicated staff.

items.title: Confidentiality Scope
items.text: Must be explicit regarding trade secrets to be enforceable under the 'Unfair Competition Prevention and Trade Secret Protection Act'.

items.title: Stamp Tax
items.text: Certain original contracts exceeding KRW 10M in value may require the payment of stamp tax (e-stamps).

heroData.title: Tech Ecosystem
heroData.subtitle: Advanced
heroData.description: World-class IT infrastructure. High mobile penetration.

steps.title: Platform Selection
steps.description: Web dominates, but Mobile-First (Android specifically) is critical due to Samsung's market share in Korea.

steps.title: Localization (L10n)
steps.description: Adapting UI for Korean characters (Hangul). Note: Fonts like 'Noto Sans KR' or 'Pretendard' are industry standards.

steps.title: Payment Integration
steps.description: Integrating with local gateways (PGs) like Toss Payments, KG Inicis, or KakaoPay is essential; Stripe/Mollie have limited usage.

faqs.question: Which tech stack is most popular in Korea?
faqs.answer: Java with Spring Boot is the de-facto standard for enterprise, while React and TypeScript are dominant for frontend.

faqs.question: Is it hard to hire AI engineers in Seoul?
faqs.answer: Yes, competition from Kakao, Naver, and Samsung is intense. Expect to pay a 20-30% premium over standard senior developer rates.

faqs.question: Do Korean developers speak English?
faqs.answer: Fluency varies. While technical reading/writing is high, verbal communication for daily standups often requires a bilingual project manager.

items.title: Server Residency
items.text: AWS Seoul Region (ap-northeast-2) is preferred to minimize latency and comply with local data preferences.

items.title: ID Verification
items.text: Integrating 'Self-Authentication' (Phone/I-PIN) is mandatory for any service involving financial transactions or high-security data.

items.title: Accessibility
items.text: Web content must follow WAAG (Web Accessibility Action Guide) standards, especially for government-facing portals.

heroData.title: Digital Marketing
heroData.subtitle: Naver & Kakao
heroData.description: Google is not #1. Naver SEO and KakaoTalk marketing are essential.

steps.title: Naver Brand Search
steps.description: Securing the top banner for your brand name on Naver. This is the first trust signal for Korean consumers.

steps.title: KakaoTalk Channel
steps.description: Setting up a 'Plus Friend' channel for CRM and push notifications. Mandatory for any B2C play.

steps.title: Cafe/Blog Marketing
steps.description: Engaging in Naver Cafes (communities) and using 'Power Bloggers' for organic reviews and social proof.

steps.title: YouTube & IG Ads
steps.description: Standard digital spend; highly effective for the 20-40 demographic in Seoul.

items.title: Naver vs Google
items.text: Google is gaining share (now ~30%), but Naver is still the destination for local reviews, maps, and shopping searches.

items.title: Coupons & Points
items.text: The Korean market is highly driven by point ecosystems (Naver Pay points, OK Cashbag) and flash discounts.

faqs.question: Why is Naver different from Google?
faqs.answer: Naver is a 'walled garden' portal. SEO focuses on Naver-owned properties like Blogs, Cafes, and Knowledge iN rather than external links.

faqs.question: Should I use KakaoTalk for marketing?
faqs.answer: Yes, the KakaoTalk 'Channel' is the primary way to maintain relationships with existing customers in Korea.

faqs.question: Is English content effective?
faqs.answer: Only for niche B2B tech audiences. For the general public, 100% localization in Hangul is mandatory for conversion.

items.title: Naver Search Advisor
items.text: Registering your site to ensure basic indexing on the domestic search results.

items.title: KCP / Toss PG
items.text: Setting up local payment gateways to enable Naver Pay and Samsung Pay at checkout.

items.title: Privacy Policy
items.text: Must include specific Korean PIPA clauses and the name of the Data Privacy Officer.

items.title: Naver Search Advisor
items.text: Registration of the website on Naver's equivalent of Google Search Console for visibility.

items.title: Kakao Business Channel
items.text: Verified business profile on KakaoTalk for customer support and lead generation.

items.title: Local Payment Gateway
items.text: Integration with KG Inicis or Toss Payments for domestic credit card processing.

items.title: KCC Accessibility Cert
items.text: Ensuring the website meets Korean web accessibility standards (often required for govt-related b2b).

items.title: Domain .kr or .co.kr
items.text: Highly recommended for local SEO and trust; requires local business registration.

items.title: Naver Maps Integration
items.text: Essential for 'O2O' (Online to Offline) businesses to show physical presence in Seoul/Gyeonggi.

items.title: Localized Privacy Policy
items.text: Must include Korean language contact details for the designated Privacy Officer (PIPA requirement).

items.title: Influencer Outreach Kit
items.text: Templates for Naver Blog 'Power Bloggers' and YouTube creators, emphasizing 'Gwang-go' (paid) disclosure.

items.title: Coupon & Loyalty System
items.text: Integration with Kakao Pay points or local mileage systems to drive consumer retention.

items.title: Brand Search Ad Setup
items.text: Exclusive Naver ad unit that occupies the top spot for branded keywords with rich media assets.

items.title: Instagram Korea Ads
items.text: Essential for lifestyle and B2C brands, utilizing local influencers for high engagement rates.

items.title: YouTube Localization
items.text: Creating high-quality Korean subtitles and localized thumbnails to improve CTR among domestic viewers.
